lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: The deadliest arcade game ever. There's no proof it existed.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: The story: 1981, Portland, Oregon. A black cabinet appears in arcades. Kids queue for it.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Then come the claims. Seizures, amnesia, nightmares. Men in black visit, collect data, and the machines vanish.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Gloom looks for evidence. The earliest web mention is an entry on a gaming site, dated 1998 on the page but showing 2000 in archives. The first print mention is a magazine in September 2003.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: No cabinet. No chip. No 1980s article. No record of the German-sounding company named in the legend.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: But some of it is real. In 1981, two players got sick at one Portland arcade. Ten days later, the FBI raided Portland arcades. The target was illegal gambling machines.

lines.speaker: action
lines.text: Biscuit knocks a coin off the table.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: One writer concluded it was "almost certainly invented". Games called Polybius do exist now, but they were made later.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: The cabinet never existed. The legend is doing very well.
